title: Dual Citizenship for Americans: Is a Turkish Passport the Smartest Plan B?
contexts: Turkey offers a rare mix of speed, asset value and legal clarity. It is one of the few programs where your investment is a property you own. You can live in it, rent it out or sell it after three years. Turkey also allows dual citizenship without asking you to drop your US passport. That makes it a natural fit for dual citizenship for Americans. The country sits between Europe, Asia and the Middle East. Istanbul is a major business hub with direct flights to most US cities. Living costs are lower than in most US states. Healthcare in private hospitals is modern and affordable. Many US investors also value the E-2 visa link. For these reasons, Turkey often appears on every serious shortlist. Still, the program has strict rules you must follow closely.
E-2 Treaty Access

Turkey has an E-2 treaty with the United States. This matters most for Chinese and other nationals living in the US. Their own countries often lack an E-2 treaty. A Turkish passport can open the E-2 investor visa for them. For US citizens, this point matters less, but it adds value for family members. The E-2 visa lets treaty nationals run a business in the US. It requires a real and substantial investment in that business. Consulates may also ask how long you have held Turkish citizenship. Some apply a residence or link test for new citizens. Get advice before you build your plan around E-2 alone.

Türkiye's E-2 treaty relationship may be relevant.

The investor should seek US immigration advice before selecting a citizenship programme based on a potential E-2 application.
Can Turkish citizenship provide access to the US E-2 visa?

title: The Easiest Country to Get Citizenship in 2026: Every Legal Route Compared
contexts: Five Caribbean states run citizenship by investment programs. They are Dominica, Antigua and Barbuda, Grenada, Saint Lucia and St Kitts and Nevis. Donation routes start from about $200,000 in Dominica. St Kitts and Nevis sits at the top, at about $250,000. Real estate routes cost more, usually from $200,000 to $325,000. A new regional regulator, ECCIRA, now oversees all five programs. Processing often takes four to eight months. Grenada is the only one with a US E-2 treaty. Caribbean donations are not refundable, unlike a property you own. These programs suit people who mainly want travel freedom. Family size also changes the final price in each program.

Turkey offers citizenship for real estate worth at least $400,000. Other options include bank deposits and government bonds. The property must be kept for three years. Your spouse and children under 18 join the same application. Turkey accepts dual citizenship, so you keep your current passport. The process usually takes several months from purchase to passport. Unlike a donation, your money stays in a real asset. Turkey also has an E-2 treaty with the United States. In August 2026, Turkey cancelled thousands of citizenships over sham deals.
